summary: The endpoint normalization, cap-to-contained-triangle argument, inverse formula away from the empty-capacity convention, H_q branch selection including d=e, finite minimizer list, supremum passage, fixed-budget specialization, and all displayed rational obstruction computations check out. The obstruction is correctly presented only for the relaxed area, third-row, and centroid-incidence data and is not claimed to lie in the full chamber. However, equation (33) is literally false as a maximum statement on its q<-d branch: K_q is empty there, so no contained triangle exists and an area-zero maximum is not attained. The analogous boundary q=-d also requires an explicit convention allowing degenerate triangles. Because the candidate states neither convention, the requested audit of empty and degenerate cases has a genuine gap.
gaps: For q<-d, K_q is empty, so the set of triangles contained in K_q is empty and there is no maximum normalized area equal to 0. At q=-d, K_q is a point when d>e and an edge when d=e, so a value 0 likewise requires degenerate triangles to be admitted. Equation (33) neither defines m(q) as a supremum with an explicit zero convention nor separates these empty and lower-dimensional cases.
repair_hints: State an explicit zero-capacity convention, for example by defining m(q) as the supremum of areas with value 0 when K_q contains no nondegenerate triangle, or handle q<-d separately and allow degenerate triangles at q=-d; then retain the inversion only in the form actually used.
